raw_response:
Aiya, where do I start. I've been doing this 45 years on the same land, so it's not like I sit and figure it out fresh every spring. I do what I always do, and I watch what my neighbors are doing.

**My wheat** went in back in October like always. Right now in spring it's coming back up. I already put down compound fertilizer before planting — about one bag of the 复合肥 (15-15-15) for every 2 mu, that's how I've always done it. Now when it gets to jointing time, I'll topdress with urea, maybe half a bag per mu, depends on how green it looks. If it looks yellow I'll add more. My neighbor Old Wang sometimes uses less and saves money but two years ago his wheat was poor, so I don't want to cut corners on the topdress.

For water — the well is there but pumping costs money, electricity isn't cheap anymore. I'll irrigate at green-up, then again at jointing, and one more at grain filling if it's dry. Three times usually. If the spring rain comes, maybe just two.

**Maize** goes in right after wheat harvest in June. There's no time to waste — I'll have the combine cut the wheat one day and plant the maize the next two days. I buy the seed every year from the agro shop in town, the Zhengdan or whatever they're selling that year. Old farmers like me don't save maize seed, the hybrids don't work like that.

For maize fertilizer I put compound at planting and topdress urea when it's about knee-high. Maize in summer gets the rain, so usually I only irrigate once or twice if July is dry. With 13.1 mu I can't afford to waste, but I also can't afford a bad harvest — my son sends some money but my wife and I mostly live off this land plus what the children give us.

Labor is just me and my wife now. The children work in the city. For the wheat harvest and maize planting I pay the combine driver and the planter — everyone in the village does this, no choice. For weeding and topdressing, we do it ourselves, slowly.
